text:
maya: quick follow-up from RFC meeting — proposing a compact 'quality envelope' + fallback ledger to attach to quant profiles. goal: give runtime a tiny, auditable contract for safe low-bit serving without expensive per-request evals.
li: tl;dr? how is envelope different from today
maya: today profiles say which ops can be fp8/int8/4bit. envelope adds: measurable acceptance thresholds, ordered fallback ledger (with cost weights), and rollout rules (canary windows, automatic rollback triggers). runtime can make O(1) decisions.
zach: runtime perf note — must be cache-friendly and lockless on hot path. any checks should be simple comparisons.
maya: agreed. plan: store envelope in control-plane, push to kv cache with ttl, runtime does mem-read + simple heuristics. heavy shadow-eval/updating runs off-path and mutates envelope asynchronously.
ron: concern: tenant overrides. sales wants aggressive low-bit for savings, but we must avoid silent customer breakage.
maya: two main guardrails: 1) safety_level enum (STRICT|CANARY|EXPERIMENTAL). 2) overrides require audit trail and ops acknowledgement. also, default safe_fallback is to next higher fidelity, not jump to fp32.
li: can you paste a concrete example of the envelope & ledger we discussed?
maya: sample (illustrative):
```json
{
  "profile_id": "llama-3b-fp8-agg-2026",
  "safety_level": "CANARY",
  "metrics": {
    "allowed_perc_loss": "1.2", 
    "max_coherency_drop": "0.6",
    "max_hallucination_spike": "0.4"
  },
  "fallback_ledger": [
    {"mode": "fp8", "cost_penalty": "0.0", "latency_penalty_ms": "0"},
    {"mode": "int8", "cost_penalty": "0.15", "latency_penalty_ms": "2"},
    {"mode": "4bit", "cost_penalty": "0.35", "latency_penalty_ms": "5"},
    {"mode": "fp32", "cost_penalty": "0.6", "latency_penalty_ms": "12"}
  ],
  "canary": {"rate_pct": "1", "min_samples": "200"},
  "auto_rollback": {"enabled": "true", "trigger_loss_pct": "2.5", "window_minutes": "30"}
}
```
li: i like the ledger idea. runtime routing can pick fallback balancing envelope.cost_penalty vs latency SLO.
zach: question: who computes the baseline for allowed_perc_loss? model-owners or control-plane?
maya: baseline computed by offline evaluator at profile publish time. shadow-evals continuously refine the baseline and update envelope.metrics when cohorts are stable. updates are versioned.
ron: telemetry surface? ops needs enough to validate envelope decisions.
maya: ship these signals: per-minute aggregates for loss_delta_pct, coherence_drop_pct, hallucination_rate, canary_failure_rate. emit chosen_fallback, envelope_version, and override_tag in each inference trace.
li: ops playbook if canary starts failing?
ron: minimal playbook: 1) control-plane auto-rollback if trigger breached; 2) if not auto-rolled, page on-call and suggest rollback id from ledger; 3) mark profile as quarantined until shadow-eval finishes.
maya: RBAC: only SRE+platform can set safety_level to EXPERIMENTAL. tenant-level toggles can request EXPERIMENTAL but require signed approval and a 24-hr monitored window.
zach: impl tasks?
maya: actions we agreed:
- maya: PR with envelope schema + API for publish/override (ETA 48h) 
- zach: prototype runtime reader + lockless cache lookup (ETA 72h)
- ron: draft RBAC + ops playbook, include rollback templates (ETA 48h)
- li: update observability schema + dashboards for the new telemetry fields (ETA 24h)
dev-bot: created ticket #4827: "quant-quality-envelope: control-plane API + runtime cache"
li: one final thought 1: for multi-shard models we may want fragment envelopes per-shard or per-layer groups. that makes runtime decisions richer but increases storage/lookup cost. opinions?
zach: optional fragmentation ok if envelope size stays <1kb and k/v cache still O(1). otherwise start coarse-grained per-profile and iterate.
maya: agreed. we'll add a fragmentation flag in v2. thanks all :rocket:
